_about: Controlled predicate vocabulary for assertions. 'iri' is a local term in the nanopub temp namespace (not dereferenceable). 'close_match' lists well-known ontology terms that are close in meaning; they are hints for downstream mapping, not asserted equivalences. relation_type drives the quality checks in np_check.py (see README 'Rules').

relation_types.quantitative: subject has a measured/reported value for a metric; qualifiers.value (+unit, metric) required; the value must appear in the evidence
relation_types.comparative: subject is better/worse/higher/lower than object on some metric; evidence must contain a comparison cue
relation_types.causal: subject causes / leads to / enables object; evidence must contain a causal cue, otherwise downgrade to associative
relation_types.associative: subject is correlated / associated with object, no direction of cause claimed
relation_types.descriptive: subject has a property, is a kind of, is part of, consists of object
relation_types.methodological: subject (study/method) uses / is evaluated on / is trained on object
relation_types.existence: subject exists / is observed / is detected (object may be a setting)
relation_types.negative: subject does not have the relation (explicit negative finding); polarity negative

increases.label: increases
close_match: RO:0002213 (positively regulates) - only for biological processes

decreases.label: decreases
close_match: RO:0002212 (negatively regulates) - only for biological processes

direct.label: the quoted text itself states the assertion (reported result or explicit author statement)
direct.eco: ECO:0000006 (experimental evidence) when the quote reports this paper's own result; ECO:0000304 (author statement supported by traceable reference) otherwise

inferred.label: the assertion follows from the quoted text by an explicit reasoning step written in 'reasoning' (e.g. a comparison of two table cells)
inferred.eco: ECO:0000305 (curator inference used in manual assertion)

cited.label: the paper reports someone else's finding; the claim belongs to the cited work
cited.eco: ECO:0000304 (author statement supported by traceable reference)

scopes.this_work: finding/statement of the paper being read
scopes.cited_work: finding of a cited paper, reported here (give cited_reference)
scopes.background: general background statement, not a finding of this paper

modalities.hedged: stated with uncertainty (may, suggests, likely ...); keep the hedge in the assertion text
